articles.title: Electrifying Ambitions Meet Tough Reality in Europe
articles.description: European Union leaders are among the most enthusiastic proponents of maximum electrification to reduce dependence on imported energy commodities. A lot of EU policy pursues precisely that. Yet EU electricity prices last week surged to over 600 euros per MWh on a wind drought, and the bloc still gets over 70% of its final energy consumption from hydrocarbons. articles.title: Nvidia Without Huang: What a Pause in AI Deals Means for Metals
articles.description: Copper slid to its lowest in almost four months on Friday and was heading for a fifth straight weekly loss, with traders blaming Nvidia’s (Nasdaq: NVDA) loss of Jensen Huang for the latest leg down. The exit is a convenient culprit, but the slide started before it. Copper has dropped every week since mid-October, and Goldman Sachs called the correction a matter of positioning in AI-linked stocks, not a sign that fundamentals have loosened. articles.title: Iran War Accelerates Southeast Asia’s Renewable Energy Push
articles.description: Several countries in Asia have recognised the need to accelerate the deployment of renewable energy to reduce reliance on fossil fuel imports and support energy diversification. The ongoing conflict in the Middle East has significantly reduced fuel trade in recent months, leading to fears of shortages as countries worldwide scramble to find different suppliers and switch to alternative energy sources. articles.title: Singapore Makes a $65 Billion Bet on the Future of Gold
articles.description: For three years, the gold story was about who was buying. In 2026, it has become a story about where the metal sleeps at night. On Tuesday, the Monetary Authority of Singapore opened its national currency vault, with room for 500 tons of bullion, to foreign central banks and sovereign entities, and threw in a tax break for the wholesale gold trade to sweeten the deal. articles.title: America’s Offshore Wind Industry Is Growing Despite Trump’s Crackdown
articles.description: The United States was slow to embrace offshore wind, with its first small-scale commercial wind farm coming online in 2016. It would take another eight years before the country launched its first utility-scale offshore wind project in 2024. While many other countries around the globe were rapidly developing offshore wind projects as part of energy diversification strategies, the United States mainly pursued solar photovoltaics and onshore wind projects. articles.description: Iran is drafting next year’s budget under the premise that oil revenue could fall to zero, with senior budget official Mohammad Ghasemi telling the government on Monday to prepare for that scenario, as the country appears to be weeks away from that eventuality. Iran has loaded no crude since August 25, according to the US Treasury, and the oil it held at sea outside the US blockade fell from 88.8 million barrels in mid-July to zero by mid-October. articles.title: Trump Extends Jones Act Waiver For Another 90 Days
articles.description: President Donald Trump extended the Jones Act waiver for another 90 days on Friday, keeping foreign-flagged tankers eligible to move oil and other commodities between U.S. ports as the war with Iran continues to drive up fuel costs. The extension, confirmed by a White House official who spoke to Reuters, continues what is already the longest waiver in the shipping law's history. articles.description: The total number of active drilling rigs for oil and gas in the United States fell this week, according to new data that Baker Hughes published on Friday, with the total rig count in the US falling to 601, up 52 from this same time last year. articles.title: Iraq’s Oil Production Soars to 2019 High as Hormuz Flows Surge
articles.description: Iraq’s crude oil production hit 4.6 million barrels per day (bpd) in October, the highest since 2019, data from the International Energy Agency’s monthly report showed on Friday, as OPEC’s second-largest producer hiked output by 540,000 bpd from September. Kuwait and Saudi Arabia also boosted their October crude oil output compared to September, as rising volumes of oil are leaving the Strait of Hormuz on smaller tankers, which then transfer the crude cargoes onto supertankers in the Gulf of Oman.
